examples.text: The journalist decided to leave out certain details from her story.

glosses: To fail to do or carry out something due to oversight or carelessness.

examples.text: A friend of mine who runs an intellectual magazine was grousing about his movie critic, complaining that though the fellow had liked The Godfather (page 58), he had neglected to label it clearly as a masterpiece.

glosses: To ignore for the sake of simplifying calculations without significantly affecting accuracy.

examples.text: We can neglect this term, as it approaches zero in the limit anyway.

examples.text: Fifteen participants argued that the neglect of discourse on relationships had major implications for the ability of adolescents to acquire courtship skills and maintain relationships. glosses: To leave out or exclude.

examples.text: She climbed out of the car and carefully omitted to lock it. She never left anything of value in it, and she found that it was to her advantage if people didn’t have to break anything in order to find that out.

examples.text: In the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, omit sections 146(4) and 147(3) (homosexual acts as grounds for dismissal from the crew of merchant ships).

glosses: To neglect or take no notice of.

examples.text: I’m not willing to overlook such bad behaviour.
